stories.headline: Jakob Junis: Mutual option declined
stories.detail: Junis ' mutual option for the 2027 season wasn't exercised Friday, making him a free agent, Kennedi Landry of MLB.com reports. It's unclear whether Junis or the Rangers turned down his $5 million option for next season, but the 34-year-old righty will return to free agency either way after logging a 3.64 ERA and 1.27 WHIP over 54.1 innings in his lone season with Texas. He should have little trouble attracting interest from teams in need of bullpen help, though no potential landing spot would offer him regular save opportunities.

stories.headline: Kyle Higashioka: Becomes free agent
stories.detail: Higashioka 's mutual option for 2027 wasn't exercised Friday, making him a free agent, Kennedi Landry of MLB.com reports. It's unclear which side opted to move on, though it's likely the Rangers who passed on paying Higashioka $7 million after he slashed .218/.306/.370 across 186 plate appearances in the majors this year. The 36-year-old backstop will instead receive a $1 million buyout and attempt to land a new deal in the open market, though he is likely to be limited to a bench role at this stage in his career.

stories.headline: Rangers' Aidan Curry: Added to 40-man
stories.detail: The Rangers selected Curry 's contract from Double-A Frisco on Friday, Joel Sherman of the New York Post reports. Curry pitched at three different levels this season and finished with a 5.02 ERA and 1.38 WHIP across 104 total innings. The 24-year-old righty is no longer eligible to be selected in the Rule 5 Draft now that he's captured a 40-man spot, and he'll likely have a chance to capture a spot in Texas' Opening Day bullpen during spring training.

stories.headline: Michael Soroka: Declines mutual option
stories.detail: Soroka declined his end of a $10 million mutual option for the 2027 season Friday, Nick Piecoro of The Arizona Republic reports. Soroka enjoyed a career-reviving season during his time in Arizona, posting a 3.41 ERA and 1.09 WHIP alongside a 114:29 K:BB over 116 innings. The 29-year-old's strong performance significantly increased his chances of securing a multi-year deal in free agency this winter, so he'll accept a $1 million buyout from the D-backs and begin fielding offers from interested clubs in need of rotation help.

stories.headline: Guardians' Milan Tolentino: Contract selected
stories.detail: The Guardians selected Tolentino 's contract from Triple-A Columbus on Friday, Tim Stebbins of MLB.com reports. Tolentino will grab a spot on Cleveland's 40-man roster after slashing .225/.328/.453 with 21 homers, 74 RBI, 71 runs scored and 18 steals across 496 plate appearances at Triple-A Columbus this season. The 24-year-old shortstop will be protected from the Rule 5 Draft now that he owns a 40-man spot, and he'll have an opportunity to compete for an Opening Day roster spot in the spring.

stories.headline: Trevor Stephan: Enters free agency
stories.detail: The Guardians declined Stephan 's $7.25 million club option for 2027 on Friday, Tim Stebbins of MLB.com reports. Stephan hasn't appeared in an MLB game since 2023 and ended the season at Triple-A with a 10.32 ERA over 22.2 innings, making it easy to see why the Guardians passed on his option. Now a free agent, the 30-year-old righty's next opportunity will likely come in the form of a minor-league deal.

stories.headline: Shawn Armstrong: Guardians decline option
stories.detail: The Guardians declined their side of Armstrong 's $8 million mutual option for the 2027 season Friday, Tim Stebbins of MLB.com reports. Armstrong appeared in 41 games for Cleveland this year, turning in a 4.58 ERA and 1.39 WHIP with a 34:19 K:BB across 35.1 innings. The Guardians didn't deem his performance worthy of bringing him back for $8 million, so they will instead pay him a $1.5 million buyout and let him enter the open market.

stories.headline: Giants' Andrew Knizner: Outrighted to Triple-A
stories.detail: Knizner cleared waivers Friday and was sent outright to Triple-A Sacramento, Alex Pavlovic of NBC Sports Bay Area reports. Knizner slashed .219/.288/.356 with two homers, four RBI and eight runs scored across 80 plate appearances in the majors this year while providing San Francisco with depth at catcher. He'll lose his place on the 40-man roster to begin the offseason but could have a chance to win it back during spring training.

stories.headline: Joc Pederson: Becomes free agent
stories.detail: Pederson declined his side of an $18.5 million mutual option for 2027 on Friday, Jesse Rogers of ESPN.com reports. Pederson had a nice bounce-back season in 2026, collecting an .816 OPS with 26 home runs over 136 contests. Because he's a platoon designated hitter with no defensive value, Pederson could have a limited market this winter despite coming off a strong offensive season.

stories.headline: Cedric Mullins: Option declined by Rays
stories.detail: The Rays declined Mullins ' $10 million mutual option for 2027 on Friday. Mullins slashed only .205/.284/.344 with 15 home runs and 21 stolen bases over 137 regular-season contests during his lone season in Tampa Bay, so it's not a surprise the Rays will allow him to head into free agency. The 32-year-old outfielder will receive a $500,000 buyout instead.
